ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle JKL, with circle R inside; the circle is tangent to the three sides of the triangle respectively, and the points of tangency are labeled M, N, O. M is on side JK, N is on side KL, and O is on side JL. The figure marks JO = 12, KM = 7, LN = x + 3, OL = 4x - 9. Reasoning: Because triangle JKL is circumscribed about circle R, M, N, O are points of tangency. The lengths of two tangent segments drawn from the same external point are equal. The tangent segments drawn from point L are equal, so LN = LO, that is, x + 3 = 4x - 9. Solving gives 3x = 12, so x = 4. Thus LN = x + 3 = 7, LO = 4x - 9 = 7. The tangent segments drawn from point J are equal, so JM = JO = 12. The tangent segments drawn from point K are equal, so KN = KM = 7. Therefore the side lengths are: JL = JO + OL = 12 + 7 = 19, JK = JM + MK = 12 + 7 = 19, KL = KN + NL = 7 + 7 = 14. The perimeter is 19 + 19 + 14 = 52.

raw_record.question_text: Triangle $JKL$ is circumscribed about $\odot R$. Find the perimeter of $\triangle JKL$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as triangle JKL with incircle centered at R tangent to sides at M, N, and O. From the image, identify JO = 12 on side JL, KM = 7 on side JK, LN = x + 3 on side KL, and LO = 4x - 9 on side JL. From the text, use that triangle JKL is circumscribed about circle R, so M, N, O are tangency points. Apply the tangent-segment theorem: tangent segments from the same external point are equal. Thus from L, LN = LO, so x + 3 = 4x - 9, giving x = 4 and LN = LO = 7. Also from J, JM = JO = 12, and from K, KN = KM = 7. Then side lengths are JL = JO + OL = 12 + 7 = 19, JK = JM + MK = 12 + 7 = 19, and KL = KN + NL = 7 + 7 = 14. Add them to get perimeter 19 + 19 + 14 = 52.
